names: UCSF Clinical and Life Sciences Building
summary: Herzog & de Meuron-designed building at 420 23rd Street / 249 Craig Ln, Block 2 of Potrero Power Station, for UCSF outpatient healthcare including a proton therapy center, laboratory space and ground-floor retail; construction started August 2025.

milestones.text: Design Review Application for Block 2 submitted to SF Planning Department
Planning Commission approves Major Modifications to building standards for Block 2 (Motion No. 21581)
Modified plans published showing eight floors (up from seven), still 130 feet tall
UC Regents CEQA findings adopted for the UCSF Clinical and Life Sciences Building at Potrero Power Station
Planning Director approves revisions to the Design Review Application

UCSF announces financing plan: California Infrastructure and Economic Development Bank (IBank) to sell more than $575 million in tax-exempt bonds to Goldman Sachs, lent to nonprofit Campus Facilities Improvement Association, which ground-leases from the UC Regents and subleases to Associate Capital
Project Sponsor submits revised plans lowering building height from 130 ft (max allowed) to 128 ft 5 in
Construction starts on Block 2 (UCSF Clinical and Life Sciences Building / cancer research center)
Planning Director staff memo recommends approval of the Design Review Application (revised plans through Oct 3, 2025 construction documents)
Design Review Application approved (Planning Director memo)
Excavation/foundation work underway; subterranean work expected to continue through 2027, vertical work to follow

Facility expected to open in phases beginning 2028 (per Chronicle); Bisnow (May 2025) separately reported construction completion by 2029, and SF YIMBY (Feb 2026) reported overall completion expected 2030

facts.value: California Barrel Company LLC (Fifth Space, formerly Associate Capital)
Herzog & de Meuron, with executive architect Stantec
UCSF (outpatient healthcare, precision cancer treatment center, proton therapy center, laboratory space)
8 stories above grade plus 2 subterranean levels
128 ft 5 in (as approved Feb 2026; originally approved to 130 ft max in 2024)

Design Review approval (Feb 2026): approx. 685 sf retail, 89,476 sf laboratory, 187,819 sf Institutional Healthcare (Non-Hospital). SF YIMBY (Aug 2025, citing Sept 2024 plans): 188,550 sf institutional healthcare, 89,680 sf laboratory, 685 sf retail. SF YIMBY (Feb 2026): 285,500 sf occupiable floor area total (182,650 institutional healthcare, 102,200 lab, ~700 retail). Bisnow (May 2025): ~300,000 sf overall.
38 Class I and 17 Class II bicycle spaces, 3 off-street loading spaces, ~190 auto parking stalls in a future district parking garage (or an interim public/private lot until it is built)

Nonprofit Campus Facilities Improvement Association ground-leases the site from the Regents of the University of California and subleases to Associate Capital, which builds it out; financed by IBank tax-exempt bonds sold to Goldman Sachs
4175/027 (per the Feb 2026 Design Review memo); the parcel was recorded 2022-08-30

open_questions: The UC Regents' approval of the project as a Regents item (rather than only the September 2024 CEQA findings attachment found) was not independently located; the exact Regents meeting date/action is not confirmed beyond the CEQA findings document.

Reported square footage varies across four dated sources (Aug 2025 SF YIMBY, Feb 2026 SF YIMBY, the Feb 2026 Planning Director memo, and Bisnow) by as much as 15,000-40,000 sq ft; no single figure is treated as final here.

Overall completion date is reported inconsistently: Chronicle (Jul 2026) says opening in phases from 2028; Bisnow (May 2025) said completion by 2029; SF YIMBY (Feb 2026) says overall completion expected 2030. Not reconciled.
The Real Deal's May 9, 2025 article on the $575M bond issuance could not be fetched (paywalled/CAPTCHA); Bisnow's coverage of the same financing was used instead.
No source found giving a signed lease date between UCSF and the developer, or the term of that lease.
